commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix(gateway) SCG MVC breaks on non standard content-type from GML responses

Spring Cloud Gateway Server MVC parses the Content-Type of responses and rejects
the GML 2 and GML 3.1 media types required by the OGC specifications, such as
"text/xml; subtype=gml/3.1.1" and "application/vnd.ogc.gml/3.1.1".

Since 3.0.0 every WFS 1.x GML response, WMS GML GetFeatureInfo and WPS raw feature
collection answered with HTTP 500 through the gateway (#1002).

The gateway now relays a response with an unparsable Content-Type unchanged,
with the header forwarded verbatim, while parseable responses keep the default
behavior.

on-behalf-of: @camptocamp <info@camptocamp.com>

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
test: Catch tile layer removals that leave the stored configuration behind

The tile layer lifecycle assertions looked a tile layer up by name before
removing its layer. A lookup by name resolves the layer published by the tile
layer and keeps that result, which leaves the tile layer resolvable even once
its layer is gone. The assertions about the removal passed against a build that
left the stored configuration behind.

Check the tile layer storage after removing a layer with no lookup beforehand,
and cover the removal after a lookup as well.

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
Stop layer deletions from leaving their tile layers behind

Force deleting a layer to delete its tile layer, drop its cached tiles,
and evict it from the other services.

fd35e636c, from #914 and its backports introduced a bug where deleting a layer
left its tile layer configuration behind on the data-directory backend,
tied to the id of a layer that no longer exists and still holding its name.
A client recreating layers by DELETE followed by POST accumulated one orphan per
round, each contending for the name with the tile layer of the recreated layer.

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix: Gateway double-encodes non-ASCII characters in browser form posts

Declare UTF-8 as the request encoding of form posts that do not specify a charset,
right before Spring Cloud Gateway's FormFilter rebuilds their body.

FormFilter parses the body through Tomcat, which falls back to ISO-8859-1 without a charset,
and re-encodes it as UTF-8, mangling non-ASCII characters on the way to the backend services.

Browser form submissions never declare a charset, while Wicket Ajax requests do, hence Save
corrupted a title that Apply kept intact.

Fixes #981

on-behalf-of: @multiversio <info@multivers.io>

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
Skip caching a value loaded before a concurrent eviction of its key

Keep an eviction counter that get(), getByName() and the default lookups read before loading,
and only cache the result when no eviction happened in between.
The value is still returned, and the next request loads it again.

cache.get(key, loader) did more than avoid recursion: an eviction for a key being
loaded had to wait, and then removed the freshly loaded entry.

Remote events rely on that. Another pod changes an object, the event evicts it here,
and the next request reads the new version.

With load-then-put, an eviction arriving mid-load finds nothing to remove, and the
old value is cached afterwards until the object changes again, leaving the pod
serving the stale version.

on-behalf-of: @multiversio <info@multivers.io>

commits.author: Jurgis Pods
commits.message:
fix: Prevent "IllegalStateException: Recursive update" errors in pgconfig cache

Loading a nested LayerGroupInfo re-enters CachingCatalogFacadeContainmentSupport.get(),
which Cache.get(Object, Callable) forbids: the backing ConcurrentHashMap throws
'IllegalStateException: Recursive update' when the nested key falls in the bin the outer load
reserved, failing cascade layer deletes and layer group queries.

This is fixed if we run the loader outside the cache's compute function, as getByName() already does.

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix: Gateway returns 500 when query values contain a bare equals sign

Build the stripped URI in StripBasePath from the raw request components
instead of delegating to Spring Cloud Gateway's stripPrefix.

The upstream version rebuilds the URI with UriComponentsBuilder.build(true),
its validation rejects a bare '=' inside a query value, as in `CQL_FILTER=a=1`
or `viewparams=a:b=c`, and the whole request fails with a 500 that the service
itself would have accepted. Keep recording the original URL though, the
X-Forwarded-Prefix header depends on it.

Fixes #693

on-behalf-of: @multiversio <info@multivers.io>

commits.author: Jurgis Pods
commits.message:
fix: Preserve the workspace of a style referenced across workspaces in pgconfig

CatalogInfoRowMapper.loadStyle() adopted the row's workspace column for the style it
decoded. That column holds the queried object's workspace, so a layer referencing a style
from another workspace came back with the style renamed to <layerWorkspace>:<styleName>.

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix: Bus events dropped for layer group changes with default styles

Encode a resolving proxy without reference as null, like done by the creation event,
and cover the patch round trip.

XStream builds a ResolvingProxy with an empty reference for an empty <style/> element as
the placeholder for a layer group's default style, and the modification patch is built
before the catalog resolves it to null.

The reference mapper accepted the empty id, the bus mapper's non-empty inclusion stripped
it from the JSON, and the receiving pods could not construct a reference without id
and dropped the whole event, leaving their caches, GWC and datadir replicas stale.

Fixes #986

on-behalf-of: @multiversio <info@multivers.io>

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix: Default style change ignored by pods on warm catalog cache

Make the cascade match the modified layer itself, and cover the id-and-name
eviction path and the remote event in the cache tests.

Catalog.getLayerByName(prefixedName) resolves the resource and then
calls getLayers(resource), and the caching facade keeps that list under
a per-resource key. The eviction caused by a remote CatalogInfoModified
event only cascades to cached objects that can reference the modified layer,
and the predicate admitted layer groups alone. A pod that had already
served a layer kept rendering it with the previous default style, unless
an unrelated change evicted the list.

Fixes #781

on-behalf-of: @multiversio <info@multivers.io>

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:

Resolve the collections first, assign default styles to layer groups
added without styles, otherwise it reaches the catalog with a null

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
fix: User creation via WebUI not propagated to REST API

Broadcast user, group and role changes over the event bus.

The security manager only published SecurityConfigChanged when a security
service configuration was saved, saving a user group or role store go
through a different path.

Add the UsersAndGroupsChanged and RolesChanged events, and decorate the
user group and role services loaded through the security manager with
event firing and handling stores. On the receiving side reload only the named
service instead of the whole security configuration.

The new events extend GeoServerEvent directly: a user or role change
alters nothing described by a capabilities document, and must neither
bump the update sequence nor evict the configuration caches.

Fixes #702

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
Register XStream persister initializers in every service

The restconfig service lacked XStreamPersister initializers that handle
complext metadatamap values, because they were only reachable through
service-conditionals on the services that used them.

For example:
- a GET plus PUT round trip on /rest/services/wfs/settings
replaced the OGC API Features conformance object with a string and broke
the WFS service with a ClassCastException.
- Cascaded stored query configurations and OGC API link were corrupted same way
- TheINSPIRE initializer was not registered at all.

Use an auto-configuration conditional on class only for the initializers,
contributed by the owning modules and excluded from the transpiled
service configuration.

Also adds the missing propertySelection field to the Jackson conformances
module, which silently dropped it on the pgconfig backend.

Fixes #872

commits.author: Gabriel Roldan
commits.message:
Upgrade to latest GeoServer 3.1.x

Upstream moved jakarta.servlet-api to provided scopei and broke
gs-spring-configuration: annotationProcessorPaths resolves its own
dependency tree, where provided scope is not transitive, leaving the
transpiler without the servlet API it needs to reflect on constructor
signatures. Declare it explicitly as a processor path.

Also stop the transpiler from initializing the classes it loads. It only
reads signatures, assignability and identity, none of which need a static
initializer to run; initializing them executes application code at
annotation-processing time, which reaches for runtime services the
processor classpath does not provide.
